Per-condition correlation heterogeneous: session_invalidation+optional_field_addition r=-0.314 (p=0.014) is the most negative; permission_boundary conditions r=0.000 (constant behavioral score). Pooled r=0.034 is the confirmatory measure per parent preregistration

Permission_boundary conditions have constant behavioral scores (b_std=0.0) because all 60 samples produce identical behavioral signal for the same drift pattern — the pooled r is dominated by session_invalidation conditions
validity_notes: This is a frozen statistical reanalysis of parent EXP-GRAPH-35308806969 raw_evidence. No new HTTP requests or server interactions were performed
TOST/CI computation uses standard Fisher z-transform: z = 0.5*ln((1+r)/(1-r)), SE = 1/sqrt(n-3), CI = tanh(z +/- z_alpha * SE)
The CI-based decision rule uses two-sided 95% CI (z=1.96), which is more conservative than TOST (z=1.645 per side). This explains the delta=0.12 discrepancy where TOST passes but CI bound fails

The pooled correlation is computed across all 8 co-occurring conditions (480 paired samples). Per-condition correlations range from r=-0.314 (p=0.014, n=60, one significant among 8 tests) to r=0.000 (constant behavioral). Pooling is appropriate for the product-relevant question of overall signal independence

Permission_boundary conditions contribute zero behavioral variance (b_std=0.0 for all 4 PB conditions), so they do not contribute to the pooled r. The pooled r is entirely determined by the 4 session_invalidation conditions (240 samples)

Fisher z-transform assumes bivariate normality. Behavioral scores are bounded [0, 5] and structural scores are bounded [0, 6], which introduces mild non-normality. The approximation is adequate for n=480 with near-zero r
unresolved: Whether the pooled r=0.034 driven entirely by session_invalidation conditions (240/480 samples) represents true signal correlation or artifact of the graded session_status_check mapping (401->1.0, 403->0.5, 500->0.75)
Whether the single significant per-condition r=-0.314 on SI+optional_field_addition replicates or is sampling noise (1/8 expected under null; binomial p=0.031 for exactly 1 significant at alpha=0.05)
Whether the delta=0.15 equivalence margin is acceptable for product architecture decisions (delta=0.15 corresponds to <2.25% shared variance, meaning >97.75% of variance is independent)
Whether delta=0.12 is practically required — if so, minimum n=518 (CI bound) or n=118 (TOST) is needed, and the current n=480 is insufficient for the CI-based rule
Whether real APIs with stochastic behavior (DB/cache/CDN) preserve the near-zero correlation structure observed on deterministic Flask mock
Whether alternative session_status_check mappings (e.g., continuous TTL-based) change the correlation structure
Whether the one-sided 95% CI upper bound (0.108) should be used as the decision criterion instead of the two-sided CI upper bound (0.123) — the one-sided bound would pass delta=0.12
Whether wider stochastic variation (all 7 non-empty permission subsets, larger n per condition) changes the pooled correlation estimate
